In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the North-Eastern region of Europe the R 1 a1 haplogroup was spread by the first wave of migration from Central Asia, and it was not replaced by the later waves of migration.
the pre-Copper Age population of North-East Europe was a mixture of the local hunter-gatherers and migrants from the South and East.
the North-Eastern European population was formed as a result of several waves of migration from the South, which occurred in the period of 15,000–10,000 years ago.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ancient DNA of the pre-Copper Age North Eastern Europe is characterized by the presence of the following Y-DNA haplotypes: R 1 a1a, R 1 a2, R 1 b1a1a, R1b1a2a1a, I2, I1.
the R 1 a1 haplogroup is a genetic trace of a certain migration wave of people from the South-East of Europe, which happened in the period between 6.5-4.2 kyr BP.

the ancient Y-DNA haplotypes of North-Eastern pre-Copper Age population are connected with the migration flows of the Mesolithic population of the North-Western Europe and the population of the Eastern Baltic region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pre-Copper Age period of North-Eastern European population history can be divided into two parts.
the R 1 a haplogroup was present in North-Eastern Europe at least from Mesolithic times.

the pre-Copper Age population of North-East Europe was formed by several waves of migrations, and the main one, which formed the basis for the modern population of the region, came from the East and was connected with the R1a1 Y-DNA haplotypes, which are the most numerous in modern population of the North-East Europe and in the whole world.
